title: Positive-view coverage sweep for learned semantic state addressing
question: Does exposing multiple independently corrupted positive query views per optimizer update improve the learned continuous semantic state retriever when mean negative coverage is fixed at eight?
hypothesis: H_positive_views: the current learner has learned useful but narrow noise invariance; averaging gradients over multiple positive query views should improve held-out target-state retrieval before saturating.

arms.name: views_1
arms.intervention: one deterministic noisy positive query view per positive update

arms.name: views_2
arms.intervention: two deterministic distinct noisy positive query views per positive update

arms.name: views_4
arms.intervention: four deterministic distinct noisy positive query views per positive update

endpoints.name: target_top1_recall
endpoints.role: primary — correct opaque persistent state selected

endpoints.name: target_rank_mean
endpoints.role: secondary — mean rank of correct target state

endpoints.name: training_updates
endpoints.role: secondary — optimizer updates; fixed across arms

endpoints.name: negative_evaluations_total
endpoints.role: secondary — negative scoring evaluations during training

endpoints.name: positive_view_evaluations_total
endpoints.role: secondary — noisy positive query evaluations during training

endpoints.name: state_build_macs
endpoints.role: audit — one-time cached state embedding arithmetic

decision_rule.condition: views_4 recall >= views_1 recall + 0.15 and views_4 recall >= 0.50
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that richer positive-view coverage materially improves the current semantic retriever
decision_rule.does_not_license: optimal positive-view count or general semantic invariance

decision_rule.condition: views_4 recall is within 0.05 absolute of views_1 recall
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that additional positive-view coverage is largely saturated under this learner
decision_rule.does_not_license: that different positive transformations would not help

decision_rule.condition: views_4 recall improves over views_1 by >0.05 but <0.15, or reaches neither 0.50 nor the strong delta threshold
decision_rule.licenses: partial evidence that positive-view coverage contributes to retrieval quality

held_constant: H=64 task anchor and A1 H-invariant query/state stream
one optimizer update per positive code per epoch
same deterministic positive-view transformation for a given seed/epoch/index across arms
no evaluation address or gold target enters training
prior C5 and negative-coverage results remain frozen
